newsitem.title: CANADA: Indonesia says Bre-X won't hurt ties with Canada.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says Bre-X won't hurt ties with Canada.

text.p: The scandal linked to Bre-X Minerals Ltd in Indonesia will not hurt trade ties between Canada and Indonesia, Indonesian Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo said on Friday.
Ariwibowo said he and Canadian Trade Minister Art Eggleton discussed Bre-X and decided to treat the fraudulent mining scheme as an isolated incident.

"We just tried to isolate this case so that it will not interfere with the bilateral relationship between Indonesia and Canada," Ariwibowo told reporters after meeting Eggleton. The two ministers met on the fringes of an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation trade ministers' forum in Montreal.
He said Indonesia was not taking responsibility for the fraud.
"It happened not on the Indonesian side but on the Canadian side," Ariwibowo said. "I see from the media that it is a corporate problem really."

On Sunday, a consultant hired by Bre-X found that assays from Bre-X's Busang site in Indonesia were falsified and that the deposit once considered the gold find of the century contained no gold worth mining.
Ariwibowo said Indonesia was still open to investment from Canadian mining companies since they were known for their expertise.
He pointed to Inco Ltd, which has a large nickel mine in Indonesia.
"We would like to see another International Nickel Co in Indonesia, not another Bre-X," Ariwibowo told reporters.
He said he did not discuss with Eggleton any investigations into the Bre-X affair.
He said he doubted that the scandal would hurt trade and investment in Indonesia.
